solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gossip involving Cameron lands government in it

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the jumbled letters
to involve is to entangle or twist together, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A political tittle-tattle story in which David Cameron brings the government down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lands' looks like a verb in the story but is fodder; 'involving' scrambles the letters and 'in it' places G within.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a person: someone who spreads tittle-tattle and rumour about others.

clue.text: Two slices of tripe eaten by lively Chester gathering occasioning ambulance crew?

indicators.note: the first piece is swallowed inside the jumbled city name
lively suggests the letters of the city name are jumping about into a new order
the opening two letters are cut from the word tripe

parts.note: a party is a social gathering

explanation.surface: A rowdy dinner in Chester where tripe is served ends with medics being called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lively' scrambles the city; 'eaten by' takes in 'Two slices of' tripe; 'gathering' supplies the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A team carrying the injured on litters; the question mark flags that it is not an ambulance as such.

clue.text: Politician in drink is expansive

indicators.note: the politician's abbreviation goes inside the word for drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician with a drink inside becomes talkative and generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something generous in size or plentiful.

clue.text: Garibaldis in her Italian cases cast aside by Will

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the phrase holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: An Italian woman keeps her Garibaldi biscuits in tins.
explanation.walkthrough: Garibaldis are British currant biscuits, named after the Italian general. 'Will' is a legal testament, not a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude an heir from an inheritance by the terms of a testament.

clue.text: Put up scenery with genuine character from Elsinore

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a set is stage scenery
real means genuine

explanation.surface: Stagehands erect real-looking scenery, apt for a play set in Elsinore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns SETREAL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia's brother in Hamlet, which is set at Elsinore castle in Denmark.

clue.text: Poultry parts unknown in odd stores

indicators.note: the unknown goes inside the jumbled letters
odd suggests the letters of stores are in a strange order

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Butchers' shops stocking strange cuts of poultry nobody can identify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges STORES; 'in' puts Y inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The two small tender morsels of meat on a chicken's back near the thigh carry this shellfish name.

clue.text: Chain guard up with bag? Agree to differ about this

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece
to differ means the letters take a different arrangement
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch

explanation.surface: A bicycle chain guard with a bag attached, about which two people politely disagree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to differ' jumbles AGREE, which goes 'about' CAS, the word sac turned 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The casing on a bicycle that covers the chain and gearing.

clue.text: Lecture given by agent — on edge moreover

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
a rim is an edge
and means moreover, in addition

explanation.surface: A sales agent gives a talk, moreover standing on the edge of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture someone is to scold or rebuke them formally.

clue.text: Spread provided by Peter — of age said to be ambiguous

indicators.note: ambiguous suggests the letters can be read another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peter's age is said to be uncertain, as in a snippet of gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be ambiguous' rearranges PETER OF AGE SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich goose-liver paste served smeared on toast.

clue.text: Sappers force is on ship to regain …

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
a posse is a body of men summoned as a force
SS, steamship

explanation.surface: Army engineers and a band of men board a ship to win something back.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back possession, typically of goods on which payment has lapsed.

clue.text: … leading position during initial phase

indicators.note: during means within, so the letters sit inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: a force regains the lead early on.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 9-across's surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the top or dominant rank, as in an alpha male.

clue.text: Period without Mark at home makes relationship

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: time means a period
in means at home

explanation.surface: A stay at home without one's partner Mark builds a bond.
explanation.definitionFit: A link or connection, especially one between related products.

clue.text: Spike holding dance in the edge of the wood

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the dance goes inside the spike

parts.note: a tine is a prong or spike
a reel is a Scottish dance

explanation.surface: Dancers twirl around a spiked stake at the woodland's border.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a long phrase at the end; 'holding' signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: The limit beyond which trees stop growing marks where the forest ends.

clue.text: See 12
Heads follow secondary route with veggies

indicators.note: the heads come after the route in the answer

parts.note: a B road is a secondary road in Britain
beans is slang for heads

explanation.surface: Vegetables trundle down a minor road behind the leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: A B road is a British minor road, below an A road. Beans as slang for heads, as in 'use your bean'.
explanation.definitionFit: These large flat pulses are a common garden vegetable.

clue.text: He's so distraught — being about stumped for dance partner

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece
distraught suggests upset, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A man upset at being left without a dance partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumped' is the cricket dismissal; 'distraught' scrambles the opening words and 'being about' wraps them round the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman hired to dance with patrons at a dance hall or club.

clue.text: Limeys from a long distance among spectators

indicators.note: the words for a distance go inside those for spectators

parts.note: seers are those who see, spectators
far means at a long distance

explanation.surface: Britons seen from far off by onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: Limey, slang for a British sailor, from lime juice given against scurvy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors, the original sense of the American nickname for British seamen.

clue.text: Convinced about truth? Not quite — it's a facade

indicators.note: the word for convinced goes around the shortened word

parts.note: sure means convinced

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a fact is a truth

explanation.surface: Someone sure of the truth is only half right: it's all a front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of the truth word; 'about' wraps the convinced word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An outward appearance, the outside face of something.

clue.text: As for an inclination, no dreamer he!

parts.note: re means as for, concerning
a list is a lean or tilt

explanation.surface: A man who isn't idealistic about leanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is practical and down to earth rather than fanciful.

clue.text: Oblique connection one's formed, in conclusion

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for conclusion

parts.note: a tail is the end, the conclusion

indicators.note: formed means shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sloping link has been made, and that is the end of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' rearranges ONE to OEN, which goes 'in' TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry, a nail driven slantwise joins timbers; this is that fixing.

clue.text: Beach on Ostend's front shelters old thingamajig

indicators.note: the beach comes next to the following piece
shelters means contains, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: sands are a beach

indicators.note: front means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A seaside beach at the Belgian resort of Ostend keeps an old gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: SANDS plus O, from Ostend's 'front', 'shelters' O to make S-O-ANDS-O.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are placeholder words for someone or something whose name escapes you.

clue.text: Instrument Mum's taken up is leading to extremes of emotion

indicators.note: these letters come before the next
in a down clue, taken up means read upwards

parts.note: Mum is MA and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: extremes are the outside letters of emotion

explanation.surface: Mum has taken up an instrument that makes her very emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns MAS into SAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-stringed Japanese lute plucked with a plectrum.

clue.text: Visitors using one route reported rain

parts.note: a means one
a way is a route

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: to teem is to rain heavily

explanation.surface: Visitors take one road and report a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, the visiting side playing on the opponents' ground.

clue.text: See 21
Slow start for bus on incline

indicators.note: the letter is put next to the slope
start means the first letter of bus

parts.note: a rake is an incline, as of a stage

explanation.surface: A bus slows on a hill when the driver starts.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce speed, as a driver does with the pedal.

clue.text: With southern area cleared, plant is void

indicators.note: cleared means removed, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: an annual is a plant living one year
A for area; southern picks the lower of the two in a down entry

explanation.surface: A garden plant growing where the southern part has been cleared is null.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the 'southern' A is the lower one.
explanation.definitionFit: To make invalid or cancel, as with a contract.

clue.text: See 6
Meal punctuated by suggestions of hilarity and tomfoolery in letter from abroad

indicators.note: punctuated means interrupted at intervals, so letters break into the meal word
and joins a second interruption, the first letter of hilarity also breaking into the meal word

parts.note: tea is a meal
the suggestion of hilarity is its first letter, H

indicators.note: suggestions are the first letters

explanation.surface: A tea party full of jollity and silliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suggestions of' governs both hilarity and tomfoolery: H goes after the T of TEA, and T after its E, the meal 'punctuated by' them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek letter, so a foreign alphabet character.

clue.text: A black mark against leaders of exciting race in TT

indicators.note: against means next to, so the letters follow

parts.note: B is black in pencil grading
a stain is a mark

indicators.note: leaders are first letters

explanation.surface: A black mark in the Isle of Man TT motorcycle races.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is teetotal, not the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy race.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teetotal refrains from alcohol.

clue.text: Singlet and smalls to launder? Odoriferous, them!

indicators.note: launder means wash, so the letters are churned around

explanation.surface: Underwear that needs washing smells pungent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to launder' rearranges SINGLET and SMALLS; smalls is British slang for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoratives with a pungent ammonia smell, used to revive the faint.
